key_insight: Rather than choosing the first action an LLM proposes, an agent can generate several options at every turn and use a second LLM to select one. This paper evaluates that inference-time scaling strategy for complex, long-horizon tasks; the provided abstract does not report results.
problem_solved: How to use additional inference-time computation to improve action selection in LLM agents tackling tasks that require many sequential decisions.
method: At each turn, a generator LLM produces N candidate actions.
A selector LLM evaluates the candidates and chooses one to execute in the environment.
Repeat the generate-select-execute cycle throughout the task.
impact: The framework offers practitioners a simple way to explore inference-time scaling for agents without changing the generator's training. Its practical value depends on whether better action selection justifies the additional computation, which the supplied excerpt does not establish.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: current state → N candidate actions → selector LLM → executed action.
Branch-and-highlight graphic showing several proposed actions with one selected.
Multi-turn timeline showing the selection cycle repeated across a long-horizon task.
Compute-budget illustration showing how more candidates increase generation work.
paper_title: On Turn-Level Best-of-N Sampling for Scaling LLM Agents
paper_authors: Jalaj Bhandari, Dhawal Gupta, Hongli Zhan, Zhenting Wang, Varad Pimpalkhute
